chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Ibn Fazzal, from various men, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they both said:
Disbelief in Allah the Magnificent is the disowning of a lineage, even if it was lowly.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on disowning one's lineage in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from the Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq (peace be upon them), establishing that disowning one's lineage (al-intifa' min hasab), regardless of its social standing, constitutes major disbelief (kufr) in Allah. This ruling underscores the theological weight of nasab (lineage) in Shia jurisprudence, linking the preservation of familial identity to the affirmation of divine order and social continuity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Ibn Fazzal, from various men, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that they<sup>asws</sup> both said:
‘It is disbelief in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Magnificent, the disowning of a lineage, and even if it was lowly’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from and ibn Faddal from various people from abu Ja’far and abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who have said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘
It is to disbelieve Allah, the Most Great, to disown one’s lineage even though it is very lowly. ’”
